key_insight: A centered finite-volume method combines near-lossless kinetic-energy transport with harmonic-density phase-mass fluxes and explicit pressure relaxation for weakly compressible single- and two-phase flows.
engineering_relevance: The method supports low-dissipation multiphase turbulence simulation on collocated grids, with a formulation suited to future GPU and adaptive-mesh implementations.
method: Couple kinetic-energy-preserving centered advection with conservative diffuse-interface regularization.
Use harmonic face densities to connect phase-volume and phase-mass transport and establish a sufficient positivity condition.
Apply pressure-increment relaxation with compatible cell and face operators.
evidence_signal: In inviscid turbulence on 128³ cells, relative kinetic-energy change stayed below 1.2×10⁻⁷ in magnitude at t*=8 for single-phase and density-ratio-1000 two-phase cases; matched upwind runs retained only 3.60% and 30.72% of initial energy, respectively.
watch_item: Phase-mass positivity and pressure-iteration energy control are conditional; GPU and adaptive-mesh scalability remain future work.
paper_title: A centered finite-volume method with explicit pressure relaxation for weakly compressible single- and two-phase flows
